concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper bound on running time as a function of input size.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Sums of coefficients times powers of a variable, with addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a+bi, with modulus and roots of unity e^(2πi/k).

concepts.name: Turing machines and tapes
concepts.gloss: A finite-state machine reading and writing cells on tapes, one cell step at a time.

concepts.name: Binary integers
concepts.gloss: Representing nonnegative integers as bit strings, most significant bit first.

concepts.name: Fixed-tape Turing machine model
concepts.gloss: The model: one fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, where time counts steps and moving data over growing distances costs scans.

evidence.quote: A machine has one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes.

concepts.name: Convolution
concepts.gloss: Combining two coefficient lists so that entry k sums products a_i b_j over i+j=k (linearly, cyclically, or with negative wrap).

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Multiplication as digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Split each integer into radix-2^b digits; the product's digit coefficients are the convolution of the digit lists, followed by carry propagation.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: Linear map F_q sending a length-q vector to its averaged sums with roots of unity e^(-2πi jk/q); it turns convolution into pointwise product and is a contraction.

evidence.quote: Each normalized Fourier transform above is a contraction, since each output averages inputs multiplied by complex numbers of modulus one.

concepts.name: Fast transforms and butterflies
concepts.gloss: Computing a transform of power-of-two length in about log levels of two-point butterfly operations, each level scanning all data.

evidence.quote: the transform calculation consists of address rearrangements, signed shifts, and two-point butterfly operations

concepts.name: Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture
concepts.gloss: The 1971 O(n log n log log n) multitape multiplication and the conjecture that n log n is the optimal order of multiplication cost.

evidence.quote: Sch\"onhage and Strassen conjectured $n\log n$ as the optimal order of multiplication cost

concepts.name: Harvey–van der Hoeven O(n log n) multiplier
concepts.gloss: The unconditional O(n log n) multitape multiplication algorithm, used here as an ordinary subroutine on short inputs.

evidence.quote: Harvey and van der Hoeven reached the unconditional $O(n\log n)$ upper

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring size
symbols.meaning: A power of two giving the number of complex coefficients in each polynomial record.

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The polynomial variable, whose r-th power equals -1 in the ring.

concepts.gloss: Complex polynomials of degree below r with y^r = -1, so multiplying by a power of y is a signed shift of the coefficient list.

evidence.quote: Powers of $y$ then serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes, and multiplication by such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list.

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: A Fourier transform over the ring modulo y^r+1 using powers of y as roots of unity, so all root multiplications are exact signed shifts.

evidence.quote: These are the synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and Nussbaumer

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder map to prime axes
concepts.gloss: Re-indexing the coefficient list onto a product of distinct prime cyclic axes by the Chinese remainder theorem so cyclic convolution is preserved.

evidence.quote: the radix-digit coefficient list is placed on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Expressing a Fourier transform of prime-like length through a power-of-two multidimensional transform via Gaussian-weighted resampling, with permutations on source and target.

evidence.quote: Gaussian resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a power-of-two tensor transform.

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Rewriting a DFT of arbitrary length as a convolution with a chirp e^(πi j^2/q) and pre/post multiplications.

evidence.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform, including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution.

concepts.name: Last-coordinate phase twist
concepts.gloss: Multiplying by a diagonal phase so that a cyclic coordinate becomes a polynomial modulo y^r+1, whose negative wrap yields the cyclic wrap after the twist is removed.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$

concepts.name: Fixed-point dyadic arithmetic and contractions
concepts.gloss: Gaussian dyadic values on a 2^-p grid, one truncation per layer, and norm-nonincreasing linear maps whose errors add when composed.

evidence.quote: Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics, whose real and imaginary parts have power-of-two denominators.

concepts.name: Signed packing (Kronecker substitution)
concepts.gloss: Packing polynomial coefficients, possibly negative, into one integer so a ring product becomes one integer product, recovered exactly afterward.

evidence.quote: Signed coefficient packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Linear network with roles and frames
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network exchanging two banks of values while restoring auxiliary values; arrays on wires carry invertible frames that cancel along routes and leave an endpoint operator.

evidence.quote: Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values, with prescribed signs, and restores every auxiliary value.
We call $D_v$ its frame

concepts.name: Three-subset intersection construction
concepts.gloss: Nested subspaces attached to gates using three-element subsets, with gather/scatter and auxiliary wires cancelling unwanted intersection coefficients, giving s<Wm smaller calls.

evidence.quote: The construction uses three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted coefficients.

concepts.name: Recursive rank saving
concepts.gloss: Recursing at parameter mf with s calls on streams of volume V/W where s<Wm, so cost per volume grows by s/W<m per factor m, giving a power saving.

evidence.quote: The decisive property is that the total number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.
This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Triangular factorization of address shears
concepts.gloss: Bruhat-style factorization into lower triangular maps so a shear (H,D)→(H+D,D) of address fields is done by ordered scans.

evidence.quote: The required factorization is the Bruhat factorization for arbitrary matrices, with coordinate order reversed

concepts.name: Fast interchange of address chunks
concepts.gloss: Swapping two disjoint address fields of u digits in time O(V u^τ), τ<1, via XOR-combined intermediate data restoring an exact permutation.

evidence.quote: The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields of $u$ bits in an array whose addresses form a complete Cartesian product.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: Applying H0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2) on one bit in each of up to d address chunks at once on polynomial records in cost O(V d^λ'), λ'<1.

evidence.quote: simultaneously on selected coordinate bits of the numerical arrays.

concepts.name: Retained transform layout
concepts.gloss: Storing synthetic transform output in a layout where the parallel layers apply and keeping the frequency order so the opposite transform consumes it after pointwise product.

evidence.quote: We also specify where each frequency entry is stored, because the opposite transform consumes that same order after a pointwise product.

concepts.name: Exact normalized ring convolution
concepts.gloss: Convolution over the polynomial ring on the remaining axes: two forward transforms, pointwise ring products via signed packing, and the opposite transform.

evidence.quote: Their polynomial products use signed packing and the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier as an ordinary subroutine.

concepts.name: Resampling with permutations left in the transform
concepts.gloss: Keeping the source and target coordinate permutations inside the transform identity so no separate full sorts are run, and the source permutation cancels across transforms.

evidence.quote: We retain both permutations in the transform formula and compute that formula directly.

concepts.name: Precision and exact recovery
concepts.gloss: Bounding rounding error so recovered coefficients are within 1/2 of integers, then rounding and propagating carries.

evidence.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$

concepts.name: Fixed rational parameter choice
concepts.gloss: Conservative fixed exponents (τ, λ, c, ε, etc.) compatible across procedures, yielding κ=2^-182.

evidence.quote: These constants are deliberately conservative; no optimization is claimed.

concepts.name: The multiplication algorithm
concepts.gloss: Digits to source arrays via address map, two forward transforms, pointwise product, opposite transform, rescale, round, carry.

evidence.quote: Apply the coefficient-address map $\Phi$, with its padded layout, to obtain source arrays $u,v$.

concepts.name: Integer multiplication in O(n (lg n)^(1-κ)) time
concepts.title: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time

symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers being multiplied.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed tiny constant 2^-182 giving the power saving in the logarithmic factor.

concepts.gloss: A deterministic fixed-tape machine multiplying n-bit integers in O(n (lg n)^(1-κ)) time, refuting the n log n optimality conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote: There is one deterministic Turing machine $A$, with a fixed finite alphabet

concepts.name: Linear maps and matrices
concepts.gloss: A linear map between finite-dimensional vector spaces is represented by a matrix, and an invertible one has an inverse that undoes it.

concepts.name: Subspaces, bases and dimension
concepts.gloss: A subspace is a subset of a vector space closed under addition and scaling, described by a basis whose size is its dimension.

concepts.name: Tensor (Kronecker) product of vectors and matrices
aliases: product of operators on separate coordinates
concepts.gloss: The tensor product of vectors or operators acts on a multi-index array by applying one factor along each coordinate axis.

concepts.name: Vector norms and the sup norm
concepts.gloss: A norm measures vector size, the sup norm is the largest absolute entry, and a map that never increases the norm is a contraction.

concepts.name: Inner product and orthogonality
concepts.gloss: An inner product gives lengths and angles, and two vectors are orthogonal when their inner product is zero.

concepts.name: Triangular matrices and permutation matrices
concepts.gloss: Triangular matrices have zeros on one side of the diagonal and are easy to apply and invert, and permutation matrices reorder coordinates.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Integers taken modulo m are identified when they differ by a multiple of m, and addition and multiplication respect this.

concepts.name: Chinese remainder theorem
concepts.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli, residues modulo each one determine a unique residue modulo their product.

concepts.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
concepts.gloss: A prime has no divisors except 1 and itself, and two integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1.

concepts.name: Cyclic groups and indices mod m
concepts.gloss: The integers mod m under addition form a cyclic group, used to index arrays that wrap around.

concepts.name: Finite field F_2 and XOR
concepts.gloss: Bits under addition mod 2 form a field, where addition is the exclusive or.

concepts.name: Bit operations and address fields
concepts.gloss: Array indices written in binary split into contiguous fields of bits that can be read, swapped or masked.

concepts.name: Permutations
concepts.gloss: A permutation is a bijection of a finite set onto itself, and applying one to an array rearranges its entries.

concepts.name: Cartesian products and multidimensional arrays
concepts.gloss: A multidimensional array is indexed by tuples from a product of finite sets, one set per axis.

concepts.name: Floor, ceiling and logarithms
concepts.gloss: Floor and ceiling round down and up to integers, and the base-2 logarithm gives the number of bits needed for a number.

concepts.name: Powers of two and dyadic rationals
concepts.gloss: A dyadic rational is an integer divided by a power of two, exactly representable as a finite binary fraction.

concepts.name: Rings and the identity y^r = -1
concepts.gloss: A ring has addition and multiplication obeying the usual laws, and quotienting polynomials by a relation such as y^r=-1 gives a new ring.

concepts.name: Recurrences and recursion cost analysis
concepts.gloss: The cost of a recursive algorithm is bounded by solving a recurrence that relates the cost on size n to costs on smaller inputs.

concepts.name: Sorting and sequential scans on tapes
concepts.gloss: Sorting arranges items by key in O(N log N) comparisons, and a scan reads a tape once from end to end.

concepts.name: Schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication
concepts.gloss: Grade-school multiplication takes quadratic time in the number of digits, and Karatsuba lowers the exponent by splitting numbers in two.

concepts.name: Symbols for asymptotics: Theta and Omega
concepts.gloss: Theta gives a tight order of growth, Omega a lower bound, and tilde notation hides logarithmic factors.

concepts.name: Real and imaginary parts, conjugates and modulus bounds
concepts.gloss: A complex number splits into real and imaginary parts, and its modulus obeys the triangle inequality.

concepts.name: Gaussian function and Gaussian integers
concepts.gloss: The Gaussian function exp(-pi x^2) is the bell curve, and Gaussian integers are complex numbers with integer real and imaginary parts.

concepts.name: Subsets, binomial counts and combinatorial counting
concepts.gloss: Counting the number of ways to choose a subset of given size uses binomial coefficients.

concepts.name: Fixed finite alphabet and worst-case time
concepts.gloss: Worst-case time is the maximum number of steps over all inputs of a given length.

concepts.name: Linear independence and rank
concepts.gloss: A set of vectors is independent if none is a combination of the others, and the rank counts independent rows or columns.

concepts.name: Cyclic and negacyclic indices as polynomial wrap
concepts.gloss: Reducing a polynomial modulo x^n-1 folds high powers back onto low ones, giving cyclic indexing.

background.summary: The reader is an undergraduate computer scientist: asymptotic notation and recurrences, discrete mathematics (sets, products, permutations, modular arithmetic, the Chinese remainder theorem, logarithms, floor and ceiling), and introductory linear algebra (matrices, bases, subspaces, inner products, norms, Kronecker products). They know polynomials, complex numbers and roots of unity, basic Turing machines with tapes, and sorting and divide-and-conquer. They have not studied FFT-based multiplication in depth, abstract ring theory beyond basics, numerical error analysis, or any research on integer multiplication complexity.
